label: Sequence start on selected tokens (p,q,1,...) + first copy step (input orig(0)) in short L<=4 sequences
explanation: Update-gate unit tied to the start of the sequence. (1) At t=0 it fires deterministically (precision 1.0) when the first token is one of a fixed set of about 12 tokens (p,q,1,u,b,f,a,k,t,j,3,y); magnitude depends only on the token (p/q about 0.29 of max, 1 about 0.20, f 0.12, u/a/k about 0.09-0.10, 3/t small). It also fires weakly at t=1 when the input is p/q/1. (2) In the copy phase it fires at recall_idx==1, the step where the model feeds back orig(0) and outputs orig(1). This is nearly always active for L=3-4 and rare for longer L. These are the largest activations (up to max), largest when orig(0) is p/q/1. Smaller activations continue at recall_idx 2-3 in short sequences. It never fires on the <DEL> step, at t=2-3 of the original phase (only rarely), or at later original positions. Together t=0 and the first copy step carry about 85% of activation mass. Misses: weak t=1 activations on other tokens, recall_idx 2-3 tails, and some t=0 tokens outside the set.

issues: Missing token at t=0: when the first token is 'n', the unit is active every time (dev precision 1.0, 3216 steps, about 5% of active steps). It is left out of the 12-token set even though the t=0 rule is described as a fixed token set with precision 1.0.

The claim that recall_idx==1 is 'nearly always active for L=3-4' is false for L=4. Precision is 1.0 at L=3 but only 0.44 at L=4. Within L=4 it depends on the input token: 0.80 when the input orig(0) is in the token set and 0.21 when it is not. So the copy-phase mode is token-gated as well, not just positional.

Systematic miss at L=3: the whole copy phase is active at L=3 (phase==2 & L==3, precision 0.91), not only recall_idx 1. The 'recall_idx 2-3 tails' are left out of the predicate, but at L=3 they are a deterministic class, not scattered noise.
Copy-phase tails at L=4 (recall_idx 2-3) come mostly from inputs in the token set, e.g. a fed-back p giving 0.2-0.37. This repeats the t=0 token preference, which the explanation never mentions.
Minor: 'rarely active for longer L' undersells how clean this is. recall_idx==1 with L>=5 has essentially zero activity (precision 7e-5).

Checks that held up: t=1 activations come only from inputs p/q/1 (all t=1 activity is covered); no activity at <DEL> or at t>=3 in the original phase; t=2 is close to zero; t=0 plus the first copy step hold about 85% of the activation mass.
skeptic.revised_label: The unit prefers a fixed set of 13 tokens (p,q,1,f,u,a,k,b,j,y,t,3,n). It is active whenever one of them is the first input. At t=1 it is weakly active on p/q/1. In short sequences it is active in the copy phase: every copy step at L=3, and at L=4 mainly the first copy step when the fed-back token orig(0) is in the set.
